title: You thought the fire meant God left you.
paragraphs: You thought the fire meant God left you.
It might mean He trusted you enough to refine you.

When life starts burning,
when prayers feel unanswered,
when everything begins to fall apart—
your first question isn’t “What is God doing?”
And that’s where the lie creeps in.

That your suffering is proof of your failure.
That your trial is punishment.
That God is disappointed… maybe even done with you.

You smile in public,
but inside—you feel exposed, ashamed, undone.

the fire you’re in right now
is not exposing you for rejection—
Because Scripture doesn’t hide the fire.

“The testing of your faith produces perseverance.” — James 1:3
“When He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.” — Job 23:10
Gold is not destroyed by fire.

The impurities rise.
The hidden things surface.
The real substance is uncovered.
Let’s talk about the part nobody posts.

The secret sin.
The quiet compromises.
The pride you dressed up as strength.
The habits you said you could control.

everything you buried
starts coming up.
That’s God saving you from a life of pretending.
Because hidden sin doesn’t stay hidden.

It festers.
It hardens.
It separates.
“Be sure your sin will find you out.” — Numbers 32:23
Not because God wants to expose you publicly—
but because He refuses to let what destroys you remain protected.
You want the fire to stop.

Some scholars interpret trials as direct discipline from God.
Others see them as a result of living in a broken world.
But Scripture holds both truths together:
“And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love Him…” — Romans 8:28
Because if you stop at the fire—
Jesus didn’t just watch your suffering.
He didn’t just observe your sin.
“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24

The fire you feel now
is not God’s wrath against you.
That was already poured out on Christ.

It’s God removing what sin tried to build in you
so grace can rebuild something eternal.
You are not being exposed to be rejected.

You are being exposed
so you can be healed.
And healing requires something most people avoid:

“Lord… I see it now.
And I don’t want it anymore.”
Because grace is not permission to stay broken.
Grace is the power to be made new.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
Not that you survive the fire.
But that Jesus meets you in it—
the one reading this with that weight in your chest—
What has been hidden too long?
What is God gently—but firmly—bringing to the surface?
Because the same hands that allow the fire—
You are not too far gone.
The cross already decided your worth.
Now the fire is shaping your future.
And watch what God does with ashes.
